Subject: Post-demo: cost anchors & procurement checklist

Hi Samantha — thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and three asks so we can align commercial next steps:

1) Budget anchor: you mentioned you expect early production usage to land somewhere between 100M–400M tokens per month over the next 6 months. Can you confirm the likely monthly band (pick one): 50–100M, 100–400M, 400M+?

2) Procurement thresholds: you noted an internal PO requirement kicks in at an annualized spend of ~$50k and that P-card is available up to $10k per invoice. If those figures are approximate, please flag exact gate values.

3) Target $/1M tokens: to make a realistic proposal we need your target blended unit economics (e.g., $/1M tokens target) or a target monthly budget. If helpful, we can show three committed tiers with sample unit prices.

Next steps we propose: we’ll send a 1-page mutual action plan, a sample invoice modeling the three bands above, and a short legal/commercial checklist for procurement. Can you share: preferred billing entity, procurement contact, and any calendar constraints for approvals (e.g., Q4 procurement freeze)?

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben for pricing specifics and Connor for onboarding timing.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
E: evelyn.hart@redwood.com | M: (415) 555-0182

Hi Samantha — Ben here (pricing & economics). Appreciate the clarity on bands. A few quick notes so the MAP we send is actionable:

- Pricing model: we can do both committed and flexible (on-demand + surge). Typical committed tiers for the volumes you cited:
  * Pilot (30–60M/mo): $22 / 1M tokens (month-to-month pilot rate)
  * Growth (100–400M/mo committed): $11–13 / 1M tokens with a 6–12 month commit
  * Enterprise (400M+): $6–9 / 1M tokens with 12+ month commit and reserved capacity

- Cost levers: quantized model variants and KV caching can materially reduce billed tokens for many query patterns; we’ll include an oriented recommendation if you share a small sample workload.

- Procurement/PO notes: because your PO threshold is aligned with ~$50k/year, a mid-range committed offer (100–400M/mo at ~$11/1M) would sit above that threshold in short order — hence the procurement pathway matters. If P-card covers initial invoices, we can start pilot immediately and concurrently run enterprise buy-side paperwork.

I’ll draft a 1-page cost sheet with sample monthly invoices across the three bands and share with Evelyn for circulation.

Best,
Ben Carter
